Please answer this question with a number--which of the following best apply to the design in the study: 
        (1) totally fun first (i.e., Entertainment game reappropriated), 
        (2) mostly fun first (i.e., design workshop with disabled stakeholders),
        (3) both fun and utility first (i.e., design workshop with diverse stakeholders), 
        (4) mostly utility first (i.e., primary utilitarian mechanic designed first),
        (5) totally utility first (i.e., made by clinicians or specialists, fun incorporated later)
reasoning: The system is explicitly designed as an assistive, fabric-based interactive surface to promote free play and social/communication skills in children with autism, using a user-centered process with caregivers and contextual study in a school-clinic. The primary focus is a utilitarian therapeutic/educational goal (supporting free play for children with autism), with fun/game elements (themes, animations, music play) layered onto that purpose. This aligns best with a mostly utility-first design rather than entertainment repurposed or co-designed primarily around fun.

question:
Please answer this question with a number--which of the following best apply to the design in the study: 
        (1) unstructured play (i.e., no rules, making art),
        (2) semi-structured play (i.e., playground activities),
        (3) flexible structure with rules (i.e., improv),
        (4) flexible game (i.e., board game with house rules),
        (5) game with rigid rules (i.e., video game)
reasoning: The system is explicitly designed to support open-ended, improvisational musical free play (similar to improv) but includes structured activities with goals and some guidance (e.g., erasing smog, seeking hidden elements, following an astronaut to play a song) without penalties or rigid constraints, matching a flexible structure with rules rather than fully unstructured play or rigid games.

question:
Please answer this question with a number--which of the following best apply to the design in the study: 
        (1) entirely skill-based (i.e., trivia, sports),
        (2) mostly skill-based (i.e., mario kart),
        (3) equally skill and chance-based (i.e., catan),
        (4) mostly chance-based (i.e., Uno),
        (5) entirely chance-based (i.e., all dice)
reasoning: The system is an open-ended interactive musical free-play surface where children tap, touch, and manipulate elements to produce sounds and sometimes follow notes to play songs. Outcomes depend on the child’s actions and timing rather than random mechanisms; there is no mention of probabilistic or chance-based elements. This makes the activities entirely skill-based (motor interaction and following musical cues), not chance-based.

question:
Please answer this question with a number--which of the following best apply to the design in the study: 
        (1) entirely solo (i.e., solitaire),
        (2) mostly solo (i.e., playing against AI in single-player StarCraft),
        (3) mix of solo and social affordances (i.e., animal crossing),
        (4) mostly social, but aspects are independent (i.e., house on hill haunt transition),
        (5) entirely social (i.e., tag)
reasoning: The system is an interactive surface intended to promote social interaction and free play among children with autism, but the described activities (tapping, seeking hidden elements, following an astronaut’s guidance) are framed as individual interactions with the surface rather than explicitly multi-user or co-located social play. This suggests a design that affords solo use while aiming to support social/communication skills, fitting best as a mix of solo and social affordances.

question:
Please answer this question with a number--which of the following best apply to the design in the study: 
        (1) entirely turn-based (i.e., tic tac toe),
        (2) follows a set of steps (i.e., viticulture's dynamic turn ordering),
        (3) turns are taken, but some actions can be taken at any time (i.e., pandemic),
        (4) most actions can be taken at any time, but there are some phases (i.e., PvP death reset timer),
        (5) entirely simultaneous (i.e., race)
reasoning: The system is an open-ended interactive surface where children can act freely at any time, but there are distinct activities and in the third activity there is a guided song-following phase. This matches a design where most actions are available anytime but structured into phases, closest to option 4.

question:
Please answer this question with a number--which of the following best apply to the design in the study: 
        (1) entirely synchronous (i.e., real time strategy game),
        (2) mostly synchronous with a few asynchronous affordances (i.e., league of legends),
        (3) equal mix of synchronous and asynchronous affordances (i.e., helldivers 2),
        (4) mostly asynchronous with few synchronous affordances (i.e. cookie clicker),
        (5) entirely asynchronous (i.e., chess by postage mail)
reasoning: The system is an interactive surface where children tap, touch, drag, rip, or pinch the fabric and immediately trigger sounds and animations. All described interactions and feedback occur in real time during play, with no mention of turn-taking, delayed responses, or offline/asynchronous mechanics. This matches an entirely synchronous design.

Please answer this question with a number--which of the following best apply to the design in the study: 
        (1) entirely symmetrical (i.e., tic tac toe),
        (2) mostly symmetrical (i.e., undertale's differing NPC behaviors based on previous playthroughs),
        (3) both symmetrical and asymmetrical (i.e., pandemic with its similar turn structure but different character abilities),
        (4) mostly asymmetrical (i.e., tag),
        (5) entirely asymmetrical (i.e., keep talking, nobody explodes)
reasoning: All users interact with the same fabric surface using the same gestures (tap, drag, rip, pinch) mapped uniformly to sounds and animations. Activities are open-ended and do not assign different roles, abilities, or information to different players; the system responds identically to equivalent actions regardless of user. This indicates an entirely symmetrical interaction design.
